1: The text "The Quiet Desk" is about the use of AI in offices. The author says that the office is more quiet because software answers questions. Many colleagues like the new tools because they dont have to copy figures anymore. But the author thinks that something valuable is disappearing. He also criticises economists who say that technology creates more jobs, because young people need jobs now. The authors biggest worry is that junior staff can not learn anymore when machines do the simple tasks. In the end the author says that we should decide which skills people should keep and that companies should use AI to make workers more capable instead of only saving money.
2: The author uses many rhetorical devices to show that the issue is important. In the beginning there is a personal anecdote about the office, which makes the text more interesting for the reader. The author uses rhetorical questions like "how is anyone supposed to climb?" to make the reader think. There is also a metaphor of the ladder. In addition the author quotes a younger colleague: "nobody lives in the long run." This shows that the author is right. At the end the author repeats the idea of the quiet office, so the text has a frame.
3: I agree with the statement. Of course companies want to save money, but if they only use AI for this they will have problems later. For example when older workers retire nobody will know how to do the job because the young ones never learned it. Also workers who feel replaced are less motivated. On the other hand, small companies have not much money and must save costs. All in all I think companies should invest in their workers because this is better in the long run.
